dimensions.name: Character distinction
dimensions.definition: recognizable choices, language, attention, and silence without labels

dimensions.name: Social causality
dimensions.definition: performances visibly affect what others do next

dimensions.name: Character agency
dimensions.definition: behavior follows Character conditions rather than a hidden plot outline

dimensions.name: Relationship expression
dimensions.definition: relationships shape interpretation and behavior without numeric exposition

dimensions.name: Coherence
dimensions.definition: what happened, why attention moved, and what changed remain intelligible

dimensions.name: Earned surprise
dimensions.definition: unexpected developments remain plausible from prior conditions

dimensions.name: Assistant convergence avoidance
dimensions.definition: voices avoid collapsing into generic assistant habits

dimensions.name: Anticipation
dimensions.definition: the transcript creates desire to see what a particular Character does next

dimensions.name: Memorability
dimensions.definition: specific choices, silences, moments, or consequences remain worth recalling

dimensions.name: Mechanical invisibility
dimensions.definition: the scene avoids feeling scheduled, quota-driven, or obviously routed

blindQuestions: Which transcript feels most like distinct people?
Which makes later actions feel most caused by earlier actions?
Which preserves asymmetric knowledge most convincingly?
Is there a meaningful experiential difference, or are the outputs functionally equivalent for the purpose being tested?

unblindingLaw.interpretiveQuestion: Does mixed Performer casting enrich portrayal without replacing Character identity or destabilizing access, causal intelligibility, integrity, or deterministic authority?
